howDoI.q: How do I make a firefly that blinks by itself?
How do I stop copies of one monster blinking at the same time?
How do I draw a soft glow around a monster?
How do I make a monster drift on a wandering loop?
How do I keep fireflies near each other from blinking together?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Lightning Bugs is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. This one is about fireflies blinking over a meadow at dusk. It has two short levels. Level 1 shows six fireflies that blink and fly as one, and then six that do not. Level 2 is a meadow full of them. Each takes a minute or two.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the levels is made.

The keys

The Left and Right arrows walk and Space jumps. F2 shows your lives, hit points and score. Walk into the door at the end of a level to go on.

Nothing in this game can hurt you. For stars that twinkle the same way, see Twinkle, Twinkle; for more about glows painted in dots, see Beams and Fog.

pages.head: Level 1: In Step
pages.html:
Level 1: In Step

You start in a meadow at dusk. SIX COPIES OF ONE FIREFLY BLINK AS ONE stands beside you, and past it six fireflies drift over the grass. Every few seconds all six light up at the same moment, and they trace the same little loop side by side, like a marching band. It does not look like fireflies. NOW EACH ONE IS ITS OWN MONSTER stands where that changes. The six after it blink one at a time, each on a loop of its own. OWN TIMES, OWN PATH, NONE IN STEP stands by the door.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • A firefly is a monster. Open bugs.mbl in the monster blocks editor. The four pictures, bug.dark to bug.bright, are the same firefly with its tail dark, as an ember, dim and bright. Almost every pixel is clear (color 255), so the sky shows round the firefly wherever it flies.
  • The blink is the monster's picture list. Open bugs.mon in the monsters editor and pick monster 1, the first of the six on the right half. Its pictures go dark for 8 ticks (there are 18.2 ticks in a second), then an ember, dim, bright for 5 ticks, dim and an ember again, then dark for 38 ticks, and round again. Most of the time it is dark; for about a second it glows.
  • The drift is the monster's path. Its path is a loop of corners, each a block or two from the last, and back to where it started. It moves one pixel a tick along each side.
  • Why the copies keep in step. Each monster on the map keeps its own place in its pictures and its path, but every monster starts at the same tick, at its first picture and its first corner. The six on the left are all monster 0. They start together, so they stay together: the same picture at the same tick, the same corner at the same time, for as long as you watch.
  • The fix is more monsters. The six on the right are monsters 1 to 6. They use the same four pictures, but each has its own dark (8 ticks before its first flash for one, 48 for the next), its own flash and its own path. Three of them flash twice in a row before they go dark.
  • In the air. The fireflies pass through everything and nothing they touch happens to Mara: their pictures take no hit points, and their power is too high for a touch to pop them.
  • The sky. Six sky blocks in bands, deep blue at the top to dusky rose on Mara's row, each with its top pixel rows mixed half and half with the band above. The trees on the horizon are a picture eight blocks wide cut into blocks, and the signs and doors are copies drawn over the band or the trees behind them.

pages.head: Level 2: Dusk Meadow
pages.html:
Level 2: Dusk Meadow

A longer meadow with fireflies of ten kinds over the long grass. A FLASH, THEN A LONG DARK stands at the start. THE GLOW IS DOTS, THE SKY SHOWS BETWEEN stands in the middle of the meadow, and NO FIREFLY IS NEXT TO ITS OWN KIND further on. The door is at the far end.

There is nothing to collect. Stop now and then and watch: a few fireflies are lit at any moment, never the same few twice.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • The glow. A game has no see-through colors, so the glow is dots. In bug.bright the tail is a solid pale yellow-green, then a ring painted on three pixels in four, then rings on one pixel in four. Every pixel between the dots is clear, so the sky shows through and the glow looks soft. The purple pixels below are the painted ones.
  • Ten kinds. Monsters 1 to 10 in bugs.mon are the ten kinds. Each kind's blink takes its own time, from 57 to 119 ticks round, and no two take the same, so they drift past one another and never line up for long. Each has its own loop too:
  • Laying them. The fireflies are placed along the meadow, two every three blocks, at a height where their loops stay between the top of the screen and the grass, with one rule: no kind is used twice within eight blocks. The meadow repeats its ten kinds, but nothing near anything else blinks with it.
  • The colors. The palette has two ramps of this game's own: five shades of glow, from dark olive to pale yellow-green, and two of far trees. The grass and the earth are the Starters' own blocks in darker shades of their colors.

pages.head: What it cannot do
pages.html:
What it cannot do

These are the engine's limits, so you can plan around them.

  • It cannot start copies at different times. Every monster on the map starts at the same tick, so copies of one monster blink and fly together. Fireflies that do not need more monsters.
  • It has no random for a blink. A monster's pictures and its path repeat exactly. The meadow only feels random: ten kinds with different times, laid by a rule.
  • It cannot fade. A glow is as smooth as the pictures you draw, and there are no see-through colors, only dots of color with clear pixels between.
  • Its paths are straight lines. A path goes from corner to corner in a straight line, and every corner is a whole number of blocks from the last. More corners make a smoother loop; a path can have up to ten.
  • Nothing can follow the mouse. The game reads the keyboard and a joystick only. A monster can be made to chase the hero or run from the hero instead, but then it leaves its loop.
  • The loops drift in and out of step. With different times, two kinds now and then flash together for a moment. That happens in a real meadow too.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • In bugs.mon, change the time of monster 0's first dark picture and watch all six copies change together.
  • Lay monster 3 beside another monster 3 in dusk.map and see how clearly the two blink as one.
  • Give a kind a longer bright picture and watch a lazier firefly.
  • Draw a firefly that glows green-blue, and give it a picture list of its own.
  • Add corners to a path so its loop is rounder.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.
